description: Route a coding-agent task: which model should do it, how much effort it needs, whether its output needs a stronger review, and whether to hand it to a subagent.

model.instructions: Which is the cheapest model that will do this task well?

criteria.haiku: The default. Writing or changing code toward a clear spec or goal, even across several files: implementing, refactoring, tests, fixes with a known cause, search and lookups. Haiku writes code about as well as Sonnet. Cheapest.
criteria.sonnet: Long terminal-driven work (environment setup, builds, CI, shell debugging with many commands), debugging with an unknown cause, an unclear spec, trade-offs between approaches, or a task Haiku already failed.
criteria.opus: Rare. Open-ended design with no spec at all, or a task Sonnet already failed. Hard or sensitive topics alone (concurrency, security, unsafe code) do not need Opus when the goal is clear. Most expensive.

effort.instructions: How much reasoning effort does the task need?
criteria: medium: the normal level, enough for nearly every task, hard ones included.
high: many interacting constraints that must all be held at once, where medium has already struggled.
max: almost never; only when explicitly asked for.

needs_review.instructions: Should the output be checked by a stronger model before it is used?

criteria.true: The change touches security, concurrency, data loss or a public contract, or is large.
criteria.false: A mistake would be cheap to see in the diff and to undo.

delegate.instructions: Is this worth handing to a subagent rather than doing inline?

criteria.true: Self-contained work with a clear spec, or several independent pieces.
criteria.false: A few lines, or design work that needs the current conversation.
